title: Delivery workers made $104 million more in tips after city began enforcing new law: Mamdani
excerpt: The increase amounts to a yearly pay increase of $2,287 for each of the city’s roughly 70,000 delivery workers who drive and pedal through the five boroughs to bring meals to city dwellers’ doors, city officials said.
content_html:
Food delivery workers raked in an additional $104 million in tips after the city started enforcing a law to crack down on “deceptive” tipping practices from delivery apps, Mayor Mamdani said Wednesday.

“The days of City Hall accepting corporate abuse as the cost of doing business here in New York City are over,” Mamdani said at a Battery Park press conference.

The increase amounts to a yearly pay increase of $2,287 for each of the city’s roughly 70,000 delivery workers who drive and pedal through the five boroughs to bring meals to city dwellers’ doors, city officials said.

The City Council in 2023 passed a guaranteed minimum wage for delivery workers, now at $22.13 per hour. After that pay rate was implemented, apps including Uber Eats and DoorDash moved the tipping option to after delivery — a move the city claimed cost delivery workers more than $550 million in tips.

The apps sued to block the requirement that they give customers an option to tip at checkout, but federal judges rejected their attempts shortly before the law took effect in January.

Sam Levine, commissioner of the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protections, said that the numbers, which were revealed in a report from his department, show tips nearly doubled after the city started enforcing the law and were “proof” that the apps were wrong about New Yorkers’ willingness to tip delivery drivers.

“Far from being hurt, restaurants have seen orders surge by more than 700,000 each week, compared to before the minimum pay rate took effect,” Levine said. “This shouldn’t be a surprise. New Yorkers are consumers, but we are workers too. We want to support our neighbors who bring meals, groceries, and medicine to our doors. We want New York’s restaurants to thrive.”

The department’s report found that average tips per delivery doubled after the new laws were enforced. The tipping average is still lower than November 2023, just before Uber Eats and DoorDash changed their apps to put tipping as a post-delivery option.

Uber Eats and DoorDash did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

content_html_zh:
市长马姆达尼周三表示，在该市开始执行一项法律打击外卖应用程序的“欺骗性”小费行为后，外卖工人额外获得了 1.04 亿美元的小费。

马姆达尼在炮台公园新闻发布会上表示：“市政厅接受企业滥用行为作为纽约市开展业务成本的时代已经结束。”

市政府官员表示，此次涨薪相当于该市约 7 万名送货员每年加薪 2,287 美元，他们开车或骑自行车穿过五个行政区，将餐食送到城市居民家门口。

市议会于 2023 年通过了送货工人最低工资保障，目前为每小时 22.13 美元。 实行这一工资标准后，Uber Eats 和 DoorDash 等应用程序将小费选项转移到了送货后——该市声称这一举措让送货员支付了超过 5.5 亿美元的小费。

这些应用程序提起诉讼，要求阻止允许顾客在结账时选择支付小费的要求，但联邦法官在 1 月份法律生效前不久驳回了他们的尝试。

该市消费者和工人保护部专员萨姆·莱文(Sam Levine)表示，该部门的一份报告中披露的数字显示，在该市开始执行这项法律后，小费几乎翻了一番，“证明”这些应用程序对纽约人愿意给送货司机小费的判断是错误的。

Levine 表示：“与最低工资标准生效之前相比，餐馆不但没有受到影响，反而每周的订单量激增超过 70 万份。” “这不应该令人惊讶。 纽约人是消费者，但我们也是工人。 我们希望支持邻居将食物、杂货和药品送到我们家门口。 我们希望纽约的餐馆蓬勃发展。”

该部门的报告发现，新法律实施后，每次送货的平均小费增加了一倍。 小费平均值仍低于 2023 年 11 月，就在 Uber Eats 和 DoorDash 更改其应用程序以将小费作为送货后选项之前。

Uber Eats 和 DoorDash 没有立即回应置评请求。
